transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I wanted to get ahead of next Friday's Atlas toolkit release. As we all know, the engineering team plans to publish it in our public repository next Friday, and it includes source code, documentation, and a sample training package for external developers. Before I can record final approval, I need the checklist updates from open-source, commercial, export-control, and privacy counsel. Could each of you let me know where things stand on your respective reviews? I want to make sure we have everything documented so there are no surprises before the release gate.

This means the combined distribution must use the GPLv3 license and include corresponding source and attribution notices. I have not yet updated the release ticket with this finding. Given that this condition remains outstanding and unaddressed, I cannot provide a clean checklist update for open-source compliance at this time.

The agreement prohibits public release of that connector without written customer consent. This means the public package must exclude the connector, be limited to the core toolkit, and document the exclusion in the release checklist. I have not yet added this contract restriction to the release checklist. Given that this condition remains outstanding and unaddressed, I cannot provide a clean checklist update for commercial compliance at this time.
